"The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." That's repeated in the second half of the show, and two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. Models present the prizes.

On the planet of Krull, an evil creature called the Beast decimates the world's army and kidnaps the lovely Princess Lyssa, who is destined to become queen. Her brave beau, Prince Colwyn, leads a motley band of warriors, including Ergo and Kegan, to rescue his beloved. However, before he can face the Beast, Colwyn must locate a mystical weapon known as the Glaive, which he can use to slay the hideous villain.

Deep in the slums of Los Angeles, good-natured Felix De La Pena (John Leguizamo), a family man and armored vehicle driver, is shot in the head during a hijacking attempt gone wrong. Though his wife, Marina (Rosie Perez), offers her love and support, Felix suffers from intense physical and emotional pain following the attack. As he begins to recover, he learns he has been framed for the stick-up; distraught, Felix decides to find the real culprit himself, despite his failing health and memory.

A new convict (Stephen Dorff) struggles to maintain his sanity and sense of humanity after he's thrust into a prison system in which a brutal guard (Harold Perrineau) encourages gladiatorial combat between inmates.

Rick Wershe is a single father who's struggling to raise two teenagers during the height of the crack epidemic in the 1980s Detroit. Wershe sells guns illegally to make ends meet but soon attracts attention from the FBI. Federal agents convince his son, Rick Jr., to become an undercover drug informant in exchange for keeping his father out of prison. When young Rick gets in too deep, he finds himself seduced by the lure of easy money and becomes a drug dealer himself.

Filmmaker Terri Flores (Jennifer Lopez) is traveling deep in the Amazon jungle looking for a forgotten tribe. Terri and her crew, which includes an anthropologist (Eric Stoltz) and a cameraman (Ice Cube), come across Paul (Jon Voight), who is stranded on the riverbank. He offers to help them find the tribe, but his secretive behavior puts everyone on edge. They realize too late that he's using them to find a legendary anaconda that's worth a fortune -- if they can catch it.

Doug Chesnic (Nicolas Cage), an agent with the Secret Service Uniformed Division, is assigned to protect former first lady Tess Carlisle (Shirley MacLaine). Chesnic finds the job demeaning and a challenge because of Tess' high-maintenance personality and petty demands. He's desperate to get another assignment, but she insists that he remain head of her security detail, using her influence with the current president to get her way. When she's kidnapped, however, Chesnic's feelings change.

Liz Gilbert (Julia Roberts) thought she had everything she wanted in life: a home, a husband and a successful career. Now newly divorced and facing a turning point, she finds that she is confused about what is important to her. Daring to step out of her comfort zone, Liz embarks on a quest of self-discovery that takes her to Italy, India and Bali.

Rough and tough Geoff Carter (Cary Grant) runs a tiny airline that cannot afford to miss any flights, despite the dangers along many of the routes. When Bonnie Lee (Jean Arthur), a performer who is falling for him, sees that Geoff is preparing to fly in violent weather conditions, she takes measures to make him stay. She's successful in her attempt, and two of his employees are forced to make the flight for him -- but Bonnie may have been correct about the potential peril of that flight.

In this fact-based film, as Axis and Allied scientists race to create the first atomic bomb, British Intelligence receives shocking news of significant breakthroughs at a Nazi facility in occupied Norway. The British work with Norwegian Resistance head Knut Strand and distinguished physicist Dr. Rolf Pedersen to plan an urgent response. As a Norwegian team headed by Strand struggles to stop Nazi science in its tracks, a civilian hostage situation erupts.

During the Cold War, U.S. bomber jets are equipped with fail-safe boxes that instruct pilots when and if to attack. When an attack order is inadvertently administered due to a system malfunction, the President of the United States (Henry Fonda) must scramble to fix the mistake before the bombs are dropped on Moscow. He manages to stop almost all the bombers headed for Moscow, except for one determined pilot who manages to complete his mission, with deadly consequences.

Lt. Rip Crandall (Jack Lemmon) is entrusted with one of the most important missions of his World War II career: to shuttle an Australian spy (Chips Rafferty) into enemy territory. Unfortunately, he'll be doing it with one of the Navy's least seaworthy vessels, the USS Echo. But even in a clunker of a ship, Crandall and his madcap crew -- including his enthusiastic young ensign (Ricky Nelson) -- do their best to make their ill-equipped mission a success.

Adding to the lively comedic mood of the film are narrative song performances by Nat King Cole and Stubby Kaye.

Struggling new attorney Rudy Baylor (Matt Damon) resorts to working for a shady lawyer (Mickey Rourke), where he meets paralegal Deck Shifflet (Danny DeVito). When the insurance company of Dot Black (Mary Kay Place) refuses her dying son coverage, Baylor and Shifflet team up to fight the corrupt corporation, taking on its callous lawyer (Jon Voight). Meanwhile, Baylor becomes involved with Kelly Riker (Claire Danes), an abused wife, whose husband complicates matters when he confronts Baylor.

A rush-hour fender-bender on New York City's crowded FDR Drive, under most circumstances, wouldn't set off a chain reaction that could decimate two people's lives. But on this day, at this time, a minor collision will turn two complete strangers into vicious adversaries. Their means of destroying each other might be different, but their goals, ultimately, will be the same: Each will systematically try to dismantle the other's life in a reckless effort to reclaim something he has lost.
Movie, Thriller, Drama, Action, Mystery, Adventure

As death row inmate Matthew Poncelet (Sean Penn) nears his execution date, he calls upon Sister Helen Prejean (Susan Sarandon) to help him with one last appeal, maintaining that he is innocent of the murders of a young couple. Poncelet begins to form a bond with Prejean, and she visits both his family and the relatives of the victims, hoping to learn more about the case. As things begin to look bleak for Poncelet, Prejean does all that she can to comfort and console the hardened convict.

Frank Serpico is an idealistic New York City cop who refuses to take bribes, unlike the rest of the force. His actions get Frank shunned by the other officers, and often placed in dangerous situations by his partners. When his superiors ignore Frank's accusations of corruption, he decides to go public with the allegations. Although this causes the Knapp Commission to investigate his claims, Frank has also placed a target on himself. The film is based on a true story.

Commercial airline pilot Whip Whitaker (Denzel Washington) has a problem with drugs and alcohol, though so far he's managed to complete his flights safely. His luck runs out when a disastrous mechanical malfunction sends his plane hurtling toward the ground. Whip pulls off a miraculous crash-landing that results in only six lives lost. Shaken to the core, Whip vows to get sober -- but when the crash investigation exposes his addiction, he finds himself in an even worse situation.

A young lawyer joins a small but prestigious law firm only to find out that most of their clients are on the wrong side of the law. The company is helping to launder mob money, get clients off charges and even murder partners who threaten to blow their cover, but when the FBI come calling to gather evidence on the lawyer's colleagues, he is caught between a rock and a hard place, juggling his life and his liberty.

Josh (Breckin Meyer) videotapes his affair with another girl and accidentally mails it to his girlfriend. Discovering the mistake, he tows two of his college buddies -- and one not-so-eager kid who happens to own the car -- on a raucous 1,800-mile road trip from Ithaca, N.Y., to Austin, Texas, to save his lifelong romance.

Even though he has a new girlfriend, Andy (Preston Jones) can't stop thinking about his old high school love, Jenna (Julia Levy-Boeken), who dumped him and went on to become a high-profile beer pong model. When he learns Jenna is on tour with a beer pong tournament, he and his friend, Arash (Danny Pudi), decide to go on a road trip and follow them. After a series of misunderstandings and several encounters with the law, Andy and Arash catch up with Jenna and the tournament.

Stoners Cheech and Chong reunite and head to Amsterdam for a film festival after getting tickets from a promoter in L.A. When they show up at a celebrity party, Cheech is mistaken for Burt Reynolds, and Chong for Dolly Parton. The duo rolls with it as they roll more joints, partake in the usual antics and eat every item — which includes a lot of mushrooms — on the menu at Amsterdam's Bvlgar Café.
Two friends (Oliver James, Kristopher Turner) and a crazy Briton (Rik Young) have wild misadventures while searching for a missing girl in the woods.

D.C. is the crackpot owner of Action Point -- a low-rent, out-of-control amusement park where the rides are designed with minimum safety for maximum fun. Just as his estranged daughter Boogie comes to visit, a corporate mega-park opens nearby and jeopardizes the future of Action Point. To save his beloved park and his relationship with Boogie, D.C. and his loony crew of misfits must risk everything to pull out all the stops and save the day.

College freshmen Josh (Tom Everett Scott) and Cooper (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) are more interested in hitting the bottle than in hitting the books -- and their poor grades are set to get them kicked out of school. Their only hope of passing is to find a roommate who will kill himself. That's because an oddball college code states that a suicide victim's roommates automatically get straight A's. But sharing space with a lineup of lunatics proves enough to drive both boys crazy.

An unemployed pot-smoking slacker and amateur drummer, Anthony Stoner (Tommy Chong) ditches his strict parents and hits the road, eventually meeting kindred spirit Pedro de Pacas (Cheech Marin). While the drug-ingesting duo is soon arrested for possession of marijuana, Anthony and Pedro get released on a technicality, allowing them to continue their many misadventures and ultimately compete in a rock band contest, where they perform the raucous tune "Earache My Eye."

After their friend Billy (Anthony Starr) dies, Tom (Dax Shepard), Jerry (Matthew Lillard) and Dan (Seth Green) go on a camping trip to honor his memory. The campsite, however, has special significance. Billy believed famous airplane hijacker D.B. Cooper hid money in the area, and his friends aim to find it. Unfortunately, they are not prepared for the adventure. After falling over a waterfall, they are left to the mercy of wild animals and a harsh wilderness terrain.

When Edward Bloom (Albert Finney) becomes ill, his son, William (Billy Crudup), travels to be with him. William has a strained relationship with Edward because his father has always told exaggerated stories about his life, and William thinks he's never really told the truth. Even on his deathbed, Edward recounts fantastical anecdotes. When William, who is a journalist, starts to investigate his father's tales, he begins to understand the man and his penchant for storytelling.

The unthinkable happens when heavily armed and highly trained terrorists launch a bold daytime attack on the White House. The building is overrun, and President Benjamin Asher (Aaron Eckhart) and his staff are taken hostage. Luckily for Asher, former presidential security officer Mike Banning (Gerard Butler) is on the scene. With time running out, it's up to Banning to locate Asher's son before the extremists do and rescue the president before his captors unleash their ultimate plan.

After the death of the British prime minister, the world's most powerful leaders gather in London to pay their respects. Without warning, terrorists unleash a devastating attack that leaves the city in chaos and ruins. Secret Service agent Mike Banning (Gerard Butler) springs into action to bring U.S. President Benjamin Asher (Aaron Eckhart) to safety. When Asher falls into the hands of the sinister organization, it's up to Banning to save his commander in chief from a horrible fate.

Insurance salesman Michael MacCauley is on his daily commute home, which becomes anything but routine. After being contacted by a stranger, Michael is forced to uncover the identity of a hidden passenger on the train before the last stop. As he works against the clock to solve the puzzle, he realizes a plan is unfolding, and he is caught up in a criminal conspiracy that carries life and death stakes for everyone on the train.

Corrupt National Security Agency official Thomas Reynolds (Jon Voight) has a congressman assassinated to assure the passage of expansive new surveillance legislation. When a videotape of the murder ends up in the hands of Robert Clayton Dean (Will Smith), a labor lawyer and dedicated family man, he is framed for murder. With the help of ex-intelligence agent Edward "Brill" Lyle (Gene Hackman), Dean attempts to throw Reynolds off his trail and prove his innocence.

Early in the 21st century, technological advances have made it possible for aging, wealthy people to pay crooks like Vacendak (Mick Jagger) to go back in time, kidnap young victims like race car driver Alex Furlong (Emilio Estevez) and deliver them to the elderly clients, who then have their brains transplanted into the healthy bodies. Furlong manages to break free from his captors, but as a fugitive, he finds that the world of the future is a bleak, dangerous place.

When ambitious boxer Alain LeFevre refuses to accept a mobster's bribe, he ends up with a price on his head. A marked man, LeFevre takes refuge by enlisting in the French Foreign Legion. After traveling to a remote Moroccan outpost, LeFevre and his regiment suffer repeated attacks at the hands of the Berber rebel army. As he struggles to survive his tenure as a legionnaire, LeFevre dreams of returning to France to find his lady love, Katrina.

Brothers Kyle and Peter Reynolds were raised to believe that their dad died when they were young. Setting out on an epic quest to find him, the two siblings soon learn more about their mom's past than they ever wanted to know.

Caroline Ellis (Kate Hudson), a good-natured nurse living in New Orleans, quits her job at a hospice to work for Violet Devereaux (Gena Rowlands), an elderly woman whose husband, Ben (John Hurt), is in poor health following a stroke. When Caroline begins to explore the couple's rundown Bayou mansion, she discovers strange artifacts and learns the house has a mysterious past. As she continues to investigate, she realizes that Violet is keeping a sinister secret about the cause of Ben's illness.

Mari and her friend look forward to a holiday at the remote Collingwood lake house, but instead an escaped convict (Garret Dillahunt) and his crew kidnap them and later leave them for dead. A team of space marines known as the Rapid Response Tactical Squad, led by Sarge (Karl Urban), is sent to a science facility on Mars after somebody reports a security breach. Dr. Grimm (Rosamund Pike), who is related to team member Reaper (The Rock), informs them all that the chromosome can mutate humans into monsters -- and is highly infectious.

Queen Ravenna (Charlize Theron), who seized control of her kingdom by marrying and killing its rightful ruler, needs the life force of young maidens to maintain her beauty. However, to become truly immortal, Ravenna must consume the heart of her stepdaughter Snow White (Kristen Stewart). Snow escapes, and Ravenna dispatches a huntsman (Chris Hemsworth) to capture her. But Snow, the Huntsman and a rebel army join forces to destroy Ravenna and restore the balance of life and death.

Hellboy (Ron Perlman), his pyrokinetic girlfriend, Liz (Selma Blair), and aquatic empath, Abe Sapien (Doug Jones), face their biggest battle when an underworld prince (Luke Goss) plans to reclaim Earth for his magical kindred. Bev is back from Arizona and realizes she'd like to use her finances to spread happiness; Bev decides to fund Mark's tuition to a prestigious coding camp, but Darlene tries to convince her to give the money to Harris instead.

Dan is finally ready to share his feelings with Louise; Darlene realizes how badly she wants a baby; Ben gets caught up playing handyman and babysitter for Becky, which causes him to miss an important meeting.

Dan and Louise take their relationship to the next level and come to appreciate the complexities of aging; Darlene spends the night in jail and leaves parenting duties to Ben; Mark and a friend's class experiment leaves them both with hickeys.
Darlene and Ben go apartment hunting; Jackie and Becky take Beverly Rose on a road trip to Mexico to meet her father for the first time; Dan reluctantly shares his financial troubles with Louise.

The Conners are dealing with the pandemic and life's financial troubles; the Lunch Box is closed for everything but takeout and delivery; Becky and Darlene are both forced to search for additional income at the newly reopened Wellman Plastics plant.

Mary is devastated that Halloween has been canceled by the city, so Darlene and Becky enlist Jackie and the rest of the family to create an unforgettable experience; Mark goes toe-to-toe with a kid at school who doesn't believe in wearing a mask.

Darlene isolates herself from her co-workers at Wellman Plastics, leaving them with the impression she is an elitist snob; Louise decides to teach Harris an expensive life lesson; Jackie is determined to keep the restaurant running.

It's Beverly Rose's first birthday, but it's not all cake and candles as Becky and Emilio disagree on what kind of party they should have; Jackie is introduced to someone who wants to be more than friends.
Darlene's friendship with a manager at Wellman Plastics lands her in an awkward situation; Louise's brother tries to win over Jackie by making a thoughtful gesture, creating uncomfortable tension.

Harris' job is in jeopardy after joining a protest she strongly believes in, leading to tense discussions within the family; Jackie makes a visit to Wellman Plastics only to realize the company is instituting supervised drug testing.
Ben's mom arrives after an unexpected death and unveils shocking information from the past; Becky and Emilio spend more time together.
Harris brings home her new friend, Josh, leaving the family questioning his intentions; Becky and Ben's attempt to build a closet stirs up family drama.
Darlene earns a promotion at Wellman Plastics; Ben decides on a new career path; Jackie tries a herbal tea, and it leads to an emotional revelation.

Chuck's new purchase of a boat creates a rift; Darlene hires her first assistant at Wellman's Plastics but soon realizes she is anything but helpful; Jackie is laser-focused on her dream of being a contestant on "Jeopardy!"
Darlene starts to feel the pressures of her new job; Dan attempts to help Ben out at the hardware store, but the two don't always agree on how to run the business.

Mark is convinced he has COVID-19; Becky and Harris team up to confront Josh, who has been ghosting Harris; when Jackie visits Roseanne's grave, she finds an appalling headstone right next to it and sets out to make it right.
Chris Porter of Last Comic Standing performs his comedy routine in Kansas City.
The comic pulls no punches when discussing her childhood, culture and the transition from single to married life with her Midwestern husband.

Shot live at San Manuel Indian Bingo and Casino in Highland, CA, Jeff Garcia's Low Budget Madness stars America's rising comedy star as he not only gives a great performance on stage, but also shows you a new side of himself. Low Budget Madness is packed with hilarious sketches that will leave you in stitches and remind you why audiences all over the world can't get enough of Jeff Garcia!
Matt Braunger offers insights on the world, the bad decisions that have shaped him and how they brought him to find his better half.
Nicole Blaine bribes her husband and children to play the parts that inspire her jokes.
Taylor takes the audience on a funny and heartwarming journey that wonder chasers of all ages can enjoy together.
Papa's comedy special touches on subjects such as the hazards of churches, make-up, loose change, old age, Chinese grocery stores, raising women and magical gnomes.
The comic performs his fifth stand-up comedy special in Tempe, Ariz., focusing on COVID-19 and offering his views on mask culture, fatherhood and why 2020 was the best year to fart in public.
Yang dives into love languages, loser friends and negotiating with his Asian parents.
Comic and ventriloquist Jeff Dunham performs across five continents, accompanied by his well-known characters, Achmed the Dead Terrorist, Peanut, Jose Jalapeño, Bubba J and Walter.

The comic who has helped reintroduce the lost art of ventriloquism entertains a live audience with a little assistance from three inanimate friends who aren't nearly as wooden as their outer facades may lead you to believe.
Teamwork, talent and thrills, these group acts deliver a strong performance!

Angel says she gave John an ultimatum to propose within six months, or she'll leave; John says he wants to save the relationship but refuses to be part of anyone's ultimatum.
Daniel says Nicole is a lying cheater with a drinking problem, and he's had enough; Nicole says Daniel is controlling and constantly gaslighting her.
Maya says Tatyana is an immature cheater with anger issues and a gambling problem; Tatyana says Maya constantly nags her and creates problems that just aren't there.
Sakarreon says her husband's alcohol use spiked during the pandemic, and she is ready to file for divorce and take the children; Anthony denies he has a drinking problem.
Patricia says Arthur is stingy with his money and prioritizes his motorcycle before her; Arthur says his wife is a shopaholic and doesn't trust her with a joint bank account.
Chantel has grown suspicious of Prince's loyalty and believes she's being used for a green card; Prince says he's tired of the accusations and wants to marry Chantel someday.

Dana says she has had enough of her boyfriend's relationships with other women; she says he uses his job as a music artist to inappropriately recruit women to be in his music videos; Baxter says he's always been professional.
Caprice says Kenneth cheated and got another woman pregnant, and she's not sure if she can forgive him; Kenneth claims Caprice neglected him, forcing him to cheat.
Heidi says David is addicted to gambling and strip clubs which has left their bank account drained along with her energy to stay with him; David believes Heidi is just insecure.
Tony says Sherita wants a lavish wedding, but he wants to use that money to buy a house; he urges her to have a courthouse wedding, but she wants all the bells and whistles.
Courtney is tired of David denying their child and wants to prove that he's the biological father to save their marriage; he says that if he's not the father, he wants a divorce.
Chantee says her boyfriend of the past six years is a cheater, a drunk and extremely irresponsible; Traevon says he is sick of her spying on him while he's out with co-workers.
Christopher says Unique is so controlling she locks him out of the house if he returns home late; she believes he is cheating on her after receiving a call from another woman.
Judy says Bryan is absent from their relationship and cares only about his job; he rebuts that she is hindering his career as an artist and tries to monopolize all his time.
Lamisha says that Marcus has a habit of disappearing, he got another woman pregnant, and she suspects he's still cheating; he says she spies on him when he's with his family.
Renee says fiancé Leanthony is an angry drunk who verbally disrespects her on a daily basis; he says she is always eating, and he believes she may have a disorder.
Mary says Mike is an irresponsible liar addicted to sex-chat websites; he says her insecurities and baggage from past relationships cause him to second guess their future.
Chantell says Kevin is noncommittal and a workaholic, and she's convinced he's cheating because he's been acting secretive; he says she is extremely jealous, messy and demanding.
Elijah wants a divorce from his wife of 11 years, whom he says he caught cheating; Jennifer insists that she's not cheating, and that he has intolerably bad jealousy issues.
After finding out that Taneka cheated, Morris realizes that their 30-year age difference is a problem; she says he is terribly insecure and controlling.
Kayla says Daniel has been acting more misogynistic and shadier throughout their relationship; he says he doesn't approve of the way she portrays herself on social media.
Kyle says his girlfriend of eight years, Tai, is an unbearable alcoholic, and he is tired of her mood swings; she thinks he cheated with his "stripper friend."
Leroy says that if he doesn't check in with Amber when he's not at home, she tries to locate him and causes a scene in public; she says he is verbally abusive.
Will says Nia hates his job as a massage therapist and will do whatever it takes to make him quit; she says she doesn't trust him when he is massaging his female clients.
Brittany says Victoria is embarrassed by her and steals from her; Victoria says Brittany made disrespectful remarks in front of Victoria's family.
Laura believes Joe is a womanizer using her solely for financial purposes; he says all she does is nag and complain about what he's unable to do.
Darika says she found Brandon's second phone and one of her friends saw him out with another woman; he says he is a faithful man and her mind is playing tricks on her.
Desiree says Scott is constantly soliciting other women for sexual favors; he says she doesn't give him the attention he deserves, so he seeks attention from other women.
Monika says Kenneth is a cheater with a serious hoarding problem; he says she has become extremely jealous and calls him a cheater every time he talks to another woman.
Sandra says Theodore is a cheater who's envious of her professional success; he admits to his past infidelity but says he's in counseling and working on himself.

After a long night of dancing and drinking their way into a haze, roommates Rob (Joe Absolom), Liam (Alec Newman), Stella (Lara Belmont) and Spencer (James Hillier) and a few of their friends duck into a back room of the nightclub to play around with a Ouija board. None of the friends like what the board tells them: they will all die that night. Sure enough, one by one the young friends are slaughtered by a malevolent killer, amid revelations about satanic worship and sacrifice.
A single father (Kevin Costner) is puzzled by his daughter's (Ivana Baquero) weird behavior, which begins soon after he moves his family to a secluded woodland home.
A guardian (David Knight) and his lover (Moira Redmond) stage grim scenes to drive a haunted English heiress (Jennie Linden) mad.
An office worker becomes trapped in a building with a killer.

Years after surviving his encounter with the sinister Tall Man (Angus Scrimm), Mike Pearson (James LeGros), now a mental patient, still has nightmares about the evil gaunt mortician. Upon being released from the institution, Mike and his friend Reggie (Reggie Bannister) set out to track down the Tall Man and end his murderous and macabre practices. Also involved is Liz Reynolds (Paula Irvine), a pretty young woman who has a psychic connection to both Mike and the Tall Man.

Sonny Blake (Rose McGowan), a radio talk show therapist, moves back to her childhood home after her father dies. She is shocked to learn her neighbors are terrified of the paperboy (Daniel Ross Owens) who turns out to be a dangerous sociopath.

Anna is a cleaning woman who accepts a post at the St. Ange Orphanage. She arrives to confront an unsettling lack of orphans, save for one who acts far too childish for her age. Then the bizarre sights and sounds begin, which seem to elude detection by the only other servant or the gloomy institution's director. Is this all in Anna's mind? Or does something more sinister lurk in the heart of St. Ange?
Mónica atormenta a Belén porque se entregó a Aurelio, y le sentencia que su calvario apenas comienza. Casillas quiere volver con Robles, mientras el Chema exige a Rutila que seduzca a Rivero.
Mónica se niega a volver con Aurelio, quien confiesa que siente miedo y culpabilidad por la muerte de la esposa de Víctor. Morejón no acepta el ultimátum que los Emes le enviaron con Ignacio.
Aurelio y Tim arreglan sus cuentas a golpes. Rawlings le propone que se convierta en el mayor lavador de dinero del mundo, y también le pide que elimine al Güero, su obstáculo en la DEA.
Aurelio se reúne en Panamá con Esperanza, su nueva socia, cuya belleza y audacia lo atrapan. El Güero negocia con Tim: le dice que le irá mejor que con Rivero y le pregunta quién es su protegido.
Aurelio cae en los brazos de Esperanza y su amiga. Rivero ordena investigar los negocios de Rutila, mientras ella roba información de su computadora, a pedido del Chema. Omar alerta a Mónica.
Aurelio les dice a sus socios que ahora se dedica al lavado de dinero y Víctor queda en su lugar. Por orden de Rivero, allanan el local de Rutila y Mónica, y hallan químicos para fabricar éxtasis.
Víctor se enfrenta a Carreño y mata a uno de sus hombres: jura que eliminará al general venezolano la próxima vez que le diga traidor a su tío. Feyo le confiesa a la Condesa que asesinó a Juan.
Tijeras ataca con una bazuca a Eleazar y al general Jaramillo, y escapa cuando el ejército llega a su finca. Feyo mata a Justino y hace creer que fueron los Emes. Belén lo defiende ante Leonor.
Mónica necesita que Aurelio le consiga la droga para sus socios, pero él le pone como condición que mate al Güero. Andrews le comunica a Tim que queda frente a la DEA y está bajo sus órdenes.
Belén quiere escapar con Aurelio: sabe que Feyo mató a Justino y teme ser la próxima víctima. Los Emes atacan a Feyo, pero él cree que fue Aurelio. Víctor sigue a Mónica hasta la casa de Chema.
Silvestre intenta abusar de Leonor en casa de Elisa, pero Aurelio la salva de nuevo. Ballesteros no dice quién la rescató de las manos del violador. Víctor conoce el plan de Mónica y la sigue.
Secuestran a Luzma y sus amigos, pero Morejón ordena rescatarlos sanos y salvos. Mónica va a casa del Güero para cumplir con el encargo de Aurelio. Antes, Leonor le presenta a Andrews su renuncia.
Víctor ayuda a Mónica con el encargo, y Leonor es la sospechosa de la muerte del Güero. Aurelio culpa a Rutila por el secuestro de Luzma, mientras Ignacio descubre que es hija de Casillas.
Luzma le dice a sus amigos que su papá los va a rescatar, mientras que Morejón se entera de que Luciana es amiga de la hija de Aurelio. Leonor enfrenta a Tim: lo acusa de la muerte del Güero.
Casillas llega al lugar donde mataron a Richie, mientras Luzma ruega a los secuestradores que negocien con su papá. El Chema y el Toro descubren que Julia es la esposa de Tim y deciden matarla.

El Profesor Jirafales le regala un gato a Quico por su cumpleaños. Para su mala suerte el gato se escapa y el Chavo lo atropella con la bicicleta de Don Ramón, organizándose un tribunal en casa de Doña Florinda para juzgar al Chavo.
El profesor Jirafales les hace un examen sorpresa a sus alumnos. Don Ramón trabaja como fotógrafo en el parque y Quico por querer ayudarlo, solo arruina su cámara.
El Chavo se emociona y no puede ocultar más sus sentimientos cuando Patty le da un beso en la mejilla. Doña Clotilde se desmaya cuando se entera de que Don Ramón está enamorado de la tía de Patty.
El señor Barriga es golpeado por el Chavo y se hace pasar por muerto solo para que el Chavo aprenda una lección. El señor Barriga se disfraza de fantasma y asusta a los vecinos de la vecindad.

El Chavo y la Popis piensan que Doña Clotilde convirtió a Quico en un triciclo. Los niños tratan de entrar a la casa de Doña Clotilde para desenmascararla y decirles a todos que en verdad es una bruja.
Don Ramón ve cualidades de boxeador en el Chavo después de ver cómo noquea a Quico, y decide enseñarle a boxear.

Han pasado tres meses desde la desaparición de Plutarco, y la familia cuida de que Gaby no cometa una locura. La vida del abuelo ha cambiado drásticamente y, ahora, es un gran actor de Hollywood. Los López reciben una increíble sorpresa.

Debido a sus problemas con Hacienda, don Justo decide esconderse en casa de los López. Después de una discusión, Martina se desmaya y la Nena tiene que cuidarla. Los López tendrán que dividirse entre atender a Martina y a don Justo.

Albertano le manda a María la llave de su cuarto para que saque sus cosas, pero ella entiende que le pide que se mude con él, con su llave tiene una pata de conejo de la buena suerte, pero al ensuciarse, María la tira y le compra una pata nueva.

Doña Lucha aprovecha el corte de agua en la colonia para vender unas cubetas que tenía apartadas. María se pone celosa de la nueva ayudante del equipo de fútbol, Citlali, mientras que Albertano se la pasa en la banca por ser mal jugador.
Ludovico y Federica inscriben a Junior en el concurso Niños de Oro, donde participa cantando ópera, pues desean ganar el gran premio.
Ludovico sueña que está en una telenovela en la que es millonario, su mujer es la villana y termina casándose con una sirvienta.
Valeria sufre de bullying por parte de sus compañeros, Joaquín se da cuenta y decide defender a Valeria convirtiéndose en amigo de los bullys.
Una mujer despide a su sirvienta porque la acusa de ladrona. A pesar de eso, la empleada le cuenta a su hija que la hija de su jefa está muy enferma y necesita un trasplante de corazón.

Zulema y Oswaldo se conocieron en una discoteca, sin embargo, el plan de Oswaldo será conquistar también a Gardenia, su suegra, pues le parece una mujer muy guapa. Se descubre si Gardenia y Oswaldo se quemarán por jugar con fuego.

Esperanza tiene una difícil historia de vida. Sin embargo, Paulina, su tía, queda como responsable de ella, sin pensar que el causante de todo su dolor regresa a su vida fingiendo ser una buena persona.
Un genio inventa la forma de volver invisibles a los seres humanos, pero su creación es robada y utilizada para asaltar bancos.
Ana Leticia se entera de que Ramiro está en la ciudad. Edmundo le reprocha a Ramiro que quiera casarse con Ana Laura. Santiago lleva a Ana Lucía al lugar donde tuvo el accidente y perdió la memoria.
Lety le exige a Teresa ayudar a su padre a salir de la cárcel. Olivia le confiesa a Mónica que Margarita es su media hermana.
Gael le pide a su madre que le diga quién es su padre. Gael le reclama a Elisa por seguir amando a Damián. Carmina le dice a Damián que Gael ayudó a Ingrid a planear la muerte de Gabino.

Jeremías entra a casa de Leona. Ramsés acusa a Calixto de traición. Leona se desmaya, por lo que David le pide que se realice una prueba de embarazo. Flor le reclama a Silvano haber abandonado a su hija.
Montserrat habla con Alejandro para evitar un enfrentamiento entre él y José Luis. Pedro le pide a Nadia que vuelva con Víctor solo para que se embarace, pero le advierte que debe ser muy discreta.
Josefina descubre que Dimitrio tuvo intimidad con ella solo por interés, no por amor. Rosario va a buscar a Alejandro a la hacienda, pero María la abofetea y la echa.
Hernán le dice a Mariano que pidió una orden de restricción para Rubén y su familia porque no quiere que se acerquen a Esperanza. Vanessa, la madre de Aurora, se presenta en su casa.

Aída le dice a Rubén que Mayra quiere que le regrese todos sus negocios. Aurora le pide a Vanessa que le diga por qué la abandonó. Aída le pide a Mariano que le dé otra oportunidad a su relación y hace el amor con él.

Doña Chana le asegura a Ana Lucía que hay otras dos mujeres idénticas a ella. Soledad se pone nerviosa porque se reencuentra con Santiago, ya que antes de perder la memoria, él descubrió la verdad sobre Ana Lucía.
Bernardo le pide a Carmen que sea su esposa. Renata trata de convencer a Guillermo de comprarle un departamento a Mónica para deshacerse de ella y sus amigas.
Damián le confiesa al padre Guadalupe que él no le disparó a Gabino. Ingrid le pide a Damián que no diga que fue ella quien disparó el arma.
Benjamín e Itzel dicen "te amo" por primera vez. Leona les dice a David y Gael que no está embarazada. Leona, Consuelo e Itzel comienzan a sofocarse, debido a la llave de gas que Jeremías abrió.
Irma se recupera rápido gracias a sus amigas del cuartel y a Luigi. Por otro lado, Tomás sufre por estar lejos de Alicia y ella sigue lidiando con sus problemas económicos.
Irma conmueve a las mujeres del cuartel y a Luigi cuando les cuenta sobre su vida solitaria. Después de su pleito con Fernando, Tomás sale con Alicia, quien lo hace olvidar el dolor.
Fernando le declara su amor a Lety, pero ella sigue dudando de él; Irma recibe la visita de Rafael, el hombre que la abandonó años atrás, y ella le cuenta todo lo que se perdió.
Lety decide aceptar la oferta de trabajo de Carolina. Don Humberto y Teresita le dicen a Marcia y Fernando que les darán una casa de regalo de bodas.
Lety no sabe si hacer o no el balance para la junta del consejo; Luigi termina de preparar la última presentación para Conceptos mientras cuida que Irma no se canse mucho.
Marcia hace todo lo posible para averiguar la identidad de la amante de Fernando; el equipo celebra el premio obtenido en Cannes; Ana Leticia intenta enamorar al Borrego Nava.
Ariel se entera de todos los problemas financieros de Conceptos; Fernando y Lety celebran el premio de Cannes; Alicia le prepara una cena romántica a Tomás.
Alicia hace todo lo posible para que Tomás le dé el dinero que necesita; Lety y Fernando están muy nerviosos por la próxima junta de consejo.
Cuando Lety se entera de los gastos de Tomás, decide quitarle la chequera de la empresa; Ariel hace todo lo posible para comprobar el verdadero estado financiero de Conceptos.
Lety lee la carta de Omar donde describe todo el plan para no perder Conceptos conquistando a Lety. La junta de consejo, Lety y Marcia tienen un fuerte desacuerdo.

Toda la verdad sale a la luz en la junta de consejo; Lety presenta el balance, Ariel revela el tema del embargo y Fernando se ve obligado a explicar al comité cómo fue que se endeudó y para qué creó Filmo Imagen.
Lety se despide de sus amigas del cuartel; Marcia le exige que le muestre lo que se lleva y descubre todas las tarjetas que Fernando le escribió.
Teresita intenta tranquilizar a Marcia diciéndole que nada de lo que Fernando hizo con Lety fue por amor; Fernando le dice a Omar por qué piensa que Lety los delató.
Marcia le informa a Carolina sobre la cancelación de la boda; Lety las escucha y se culpa por todo lo que está pasando.
Irma busca pretextos para no regresar a casa, pero Luigi insiste en llevarla; Omar le dice a Fernando que no le gusta nada el hecho de que Lety haya desaparecido.
The Skeldale staff say goodbye to vet Sarah, who is leaving to have a baby; they tend to a female duck named Kevin, and a cow with a wound on its neck.
Julian helps deliver an alpaca that is in a breech position.
Alfie the Labrador has swallowed a spatula!

Julian Norton is called out on an emergency to a heifer that is in agony, with an object stuck in its painful, swollen and infected hoof; Peter removes a large lump from the head of golden retriever, Holly.

A smallholder suggests some holistic techniques to help Julian prepare his aggressive alpacas for castration; other patients include a Yorkshire terrier who keeps humping cushions, and a young lamb with breathing problems.
Julian Norton investigates an unproductive ram and patches up a terrapin at war with his tank mate.
Julian tries to save a farm dog, an albino wallaby and a cheeky pygmy goat give Peter the runaround.
The vets treat a horse with infected hooves, a cat struggling to give birth and an angry monitor lizard; they also take time out to visit the Great Yorkshire Show.

Julian is called out to a suspected case of foot-and-mouth; other patients include a Great Dane with cancer, a ram that needs castrating, a rat with a suspicious lump and a rare breed of pig that needs inseminating.
Julian treats a calf with a large and worrying lump; two pygmy goats face castration at the surgery.
Julian responds to an emergency call in the middle of the night; Moobaloo the heifer is struggling through labor with no sign of the calf; Helen looks after a seven-day-old Shetland foal.
Julian Norton treats a cat with a badly swollen eye, and helps a ewe deliver twin lambs; Peter deals with a bull terrier with halitosis.
Julian risks life and limb to inject a ferocious pig; Peter examines elderly clients Steve and Jeanie Green's dairy herd.
Julian tries to help a cow that's struggling to deliver a huge calf; the vets help a puppy that has swallowed an extension cord.
The team treat a llama with a bloody jaw and a stray kitten in need of a health check.

After a string of bizarre bank robberies in Southern California, with the crooks donning masks of various former presidents, a federal agent, Johnny Utah (Keanu Reeves), infiltrates the suspected gang. But this is no ordinary group of robbers. They're surfers -- led by the charismatic Bodhi (Patrick Swayze) -- who are addicted to the rush of thievery. But when Utah falls in love with a female surfer, Tyler (Lori Petty), who is close to the gang, it complicates his sense of duty.
Gon and Killua arrive at Heaven's Arena and advance quickly, meeting Zushi.
Wing explains the four basic principles of Nen to Gon, Killua and Zushi.
Wing's training helps open Gon and Killua's aura nodes so they can pass through the barrier; Gon challenges Hisoka to a fight, but must meet one condition before Hisoka will agree.
Gon learns the nature of Gido's techniques but still faces a tough fight, sustaining injuries and facing Master Wing's disapproval; the Agency rejects Kurapika, but a stranger makes him an offer.
After Wing bans Gon from practicing Nen, Sky Arena hosts a revenge match between Hisoka and Kastro.
Kastro's Nen double puts Hisoka at a disadvantage, and he loses both of his arms in the fight.
Gon, now recovered, continues his Nen training; Zushi gets kidnapped; Killua fights Sadaso.
Gon and Killua fight Riehvelt and Gido; Hisoka praises Gon and offers to fight him.

Kevin and Danielle are looking for a home for their growing family; they're visiting some desirable properties in Pasadena, Calif.

Carol is a salon owner who is looking to relocate with her husband and expand her business to Southern California; she tours three properties in Pacific Palisades where space for her grandchildren is a must.

Sara is looking to buy the house of her dreams in Silicon Valley; Viviana takes Sara and her friend JP through three homes; Sara wants to take advantage of the market and find the perfect home at the right price.
We meet Alex who is on the lookout for his forever home. Viviana is taking him through some the most beautiful properties in Santa Barbara, California.

Mark and Laura are searching for a luxury home; they need a house with the perfect kitchen and entertaining space.
John is ready to trade in Bay Area living for the beach and visits three properties in Orange County, Calif.
Darren and Meg are relocating from the East Coast; they're looking for better weather year round; they're visiting some desirable properties in Pasadena, Calif.

Will the sights and sounds of Venice, Calif. lure Lee and Burke into finding their perfect abode? Will Viviana be able to help them find exactly what she is looking for?
Steve and Natalie are East Coast transplants looking for the quintessential California lifestyle; we're about to see three properties in Manhattan Beach and Redondo Beach.

Tyler is leaving Los Angeles to expand his business; he's visiting some of the most desirable properties in Silicon Valley, Calif.
Amber and Kareem look to find a luxury home that's closer to his office and near the beach in the Irvine, Newport and Laguna Beach areas; Kareem primarily wants to move closer to work.
Lee's teammate, Neji Hyuga, is a talented ninja referred to by many as a genius.

Lee's beloved Guy Sensei is arrested for lewd behavior; Lee promises to clear his master's name; Kakashi Sensei's secret move defeats Guy, and Lee decides to follow Kakashi and become as powerful as he is.
Konohamaru seeks to learn better hand-to-hand combat skills; Lee and the others undergo a physical exam.
The Hidden Leaf Village is holding a sports meet; Lee is called to read the Athlete's Pledge of Fair Play, but messes up in front of the entire stadium.
Lee and his team are on guard duty at the front gate; Lee is flummoxed by Guy-sensei's new Smooth Operator Fist.
Lee's team is doing bodyguard duty for the Fifth Hokage Tsunade; Orochimaru summons Manda to swallow Tsunade, Naruto, and Guy sensei whole.
Neji's cousin, Hinata, is trying to get some training in, but Lee constantly gets in the way; Lee and several others don a familiar orange outfit.

After seeing Shikamaru and Choji in action, Lee attempts to strengthen his friendship with Neji; the Leaf ninja are scheduled to take an IQ test, but Lee's team discovers Guy sensei collapsed on the ground.
Lee and Naruto are both trying to be on Sakura's team for a research trip to the old capital city; Lee wants to slip away from all the Sensei to hang out with the girls.
Guy and Kakashi set out to teach their pupils a lesson for using their ninja skills for the simplest tasks; Lee is training in the rain without an umbrella and sees Sakura getting soaked, as well.
The ninja of the Hidden Leaf are being tested on their combat skills; Neji and Tenten succeed using their special attacks.

Lee goes to talk to Guy sensei about the issue that fewer children in the Hidden Leaf Village are choosing to become ninja; Lee overhears Tsunade saying he doesn't have much time left while on his way to visit Guy sensei in the hospital.
Lee and the gang set out to enjoy the pool, but worry they could be playing into Orochimaru's hands; Lee wants to take Sakura on a date.
Lee and the gang are out camping; Shikamaru comes up with a plan to pit the girls against each other in a cook-off; Guy sensei is in charge of running the morning exercise.
Lee and Tenten get the latest issue of "Jump" to get the scoop on the new Naruto movie; Tsunade is worried the new movie is lacking something.
The Leaf Village is holding a fireworks show, including a contest to see which ninja can make the biggest boom; Tenten starts acting strange after the fireworks show.
Teams Guy and Kakashi head to the beach; Lee wants to scope out Sakura's new bathing suit, but Guy sensei makes him train instead; Lee wants to have fun by splitting watermelons.

Gaara, the Kazekage of the Hidden Sand Village, is coming to visit the Leaf Village; an impostor of Rock Lee appears and starts causing trouble in the village; Lee's team attempts to catch him using a cross-dressing Neji as bait.

Guy sensei wants Lee and the boys to cool themselves off without any air conditioning on a hot night; Lee and Konohamaru set out to solve one of the Seven Mysteries of the Leaf, The Tears of The Great Stone Faces.
Lee and Naruto seek help from their friends the day before their summer homework is due; Lee's team visits the Academy, only to find a class full of lazy kids who mock Lee for his work ethic.
Ino catches Naruto and Lee spying on Sakura while she's bathing; Naruto and Lee end up swapping bodies after Sakura misfires her Mind-Body Switch jutsu.
It's time for the Leaf Village festival, and Lee is convinced that Sai wants to stand out more; the Mr. Leaf Village contest is just around the corner.

When Lee notices the character on Gaara's forehead has changed from "Love to Romance," he's convinced the Kazekage's got a crush on someone; Lee gets a booby-trapped watch from Orochimaru that will explode if he stops training.

Lee's convinced the upcoming dodgeball tournament is just going to be a silly kids game, until a few choice words from Guy sensei light a fire in his soul; Kabuto sets out to prove he's better than his former boss by joining Lee's team.

Lady Tsunade wins the lottery jackpot and promises to take Lee and the gang out for five-star sushi; Iruka sensei's had enough with his disobedient students, so Lee and the gang go to the Academy to put on a show.

A woman's feelings start to change when she reluctantly spends Christmas with the man responsible for ending her last relationship.
A struggling flower shop owner joins a holiday floral show in an effort to keep her store afloat. She starts to fall for her competitor, the handsome protégé of a legendary florist.
Despite busy schedules causing distance, Olivia and Prince Alexander travel to Torovia for Christmas with his family. Clashing cultures between their families lead to various mishaps.

Juliet pitches selling Christmas memory candles to her boss, and asks candle store owner Tom to create new scents. He refuses at first but agrees after realizing the money will help make his daughter's Christmas wish come true.

A fireman and a quilting teacher team up to make a Christmas quilt for the former's sister's wedding. As they navigate their feelings for each other, they must decide what is truly important in time for the holiday season.
Songwriter Brooke has the decision of a lifetime to make when a charming executive makes promises of fortune and glory that require leaving her best friend and writing partner behind.

Daisy, a determined real estate broker, inherits her grandfather's ranch just before Christmas. Focused on selling, she returns home only to reconnect with Ben, her childhood crush who now works as a ranch hand. As holiday traditions stir memories and rekindle old feelings, Daisy begins to question the fast-paced career she's built. With the season drawing to a close, she must decide between ambition and love.
If event planner Celeste Everett is going to save her business and give her niece a happy Christmas season, she is going to need help.

Jane represents a transgender student; Grayson takes on a case involving the murder of a college student; Stacy grows uncomfortable when Owen showers her with gifts; Jane decides to reveal who she really is to Grayson.

Grayson's experience prompts him to make a serious gesture; Jane offers her services to a community that is affected by fumes from a hot sauce factory; Kim must represent her mother in a divorce proceeding against her own father.

Jane takes a case involving a drunk driving accident; Stacy tries to get Owen to start living a healthier lifestyle; Kim represents a ventriloquist whose puppet is banned from flying; someone from Jane's past makes an appearance.
Jane attempts to prove the innocence of a man on death row; Kim represents a small dance company after their routines are stolen by a pop star; Owen has wedding anxiety.
Kim and Owen are unsupportive about Jane's new romance; Kim is rescued from a mugging by a masked superhero; Jane represents a mother whose son died at a football camp.
Owen and Kim try to talk to Jane about her relationship with Ian; Teri realizes that Ian is responsible for ruining her chances at stardom; Owen and Jane find themselves on opposite ends of a case.
A shallow model who is reincarnated as a brilliant plus-size lawyer after she is killed in a car accident returns to life in the plus-sized body of attorney Jane Bingum.
Deb discovers what life is like for plus-sized Jane; Grayson and Kim represent a man in a divorce case who wants his kidney back from his wife.
Jane has a difficult time controlling her emotions and is thrown in jail for contempt of court; Kim and Grayson sue a shrink.
Jane defends Deb's mother in a divorce; Kim represents a dog owner who sues a pet-cloning company.
Deb is only 24 but faces Jane's looming 32nd birthday; Kim and Greyson defend a man who created a Website for married couples looking to cheat.
Jane represents a soccer mom who is brought to trial for jumping bail; Grayson's client, an aging actor, claims the paper erroneously ran his obituary.
Jane represents a woman whose daughter begins to get sick after following a diet; Grayson and Teri defend Kim in a sexual harassment lawsuit.

A woman gives up her upscale Los Angeles lifestyle to return home to a large sugarcane farm in Louisiana after her father suffers a stroke; she reunites with her estranged siblings and learns alarming news about her husband.

The Bordelon siblings try to plan their father's funeral, but tensions rise between Charley and Nova; Ralph Angel argues with Aunt Violet about inviting his son; Charley meets someone interested in buying the farm.

After draining his life savings to enter a team in the Rucker Classic street ball tournament in Harlem, Dax is dealt a series of setbacks, including losing his team to his longtime rival. Desperate to win the tournament and the cash prize, Dax stumbles upon the man, the myth, the legend Uncle Drew and convinces him to return to the court one more time. The two men embark on a road trip to round up Drew's old basketball squad and prove that a group of septuagenarians can still win the big one.

When a no-nonsense LAPD detective (Robert De Niro) is forced to star in a reality-based television show with a frustrated actor-turned-LAPD-patrolman (Eddie Murphy), they find their lives turned upside down by a powerhouse producer (Rene Russo) and her very intrusive camera crew.

A drug operation changes the lives of three conflicted New York cops. Burned-out vet Eddie Dugan is close to retirement; narcotics cop Sal Procida faces the difficult task of caring for his large family on his ordinary salary. Undercover officer Clarence Tango Butler finds his loyalties beginning to shift toward a powerful drug dealer. Over seven chaotic days, the three men are drawn toward a fateful crime and destiny.

Clyde Shelton is an honorable family man, until the day his wife and daughter are murdered in a home invasion. He hopes for justice, but a rising prosecutor named Nick Rice cuts a deal with one of the killers in exchange for testimony. Ten years later, that man is found dead.

Following her rescue from the devastating Quarter Quell, Katniss (Jennifer Lawrence) awakes in the complex beneath the supposedly destroyed District 13. Her home, District 12, has been reduced to rubble, and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) is now the brainwashed captive of President Snow (Donald Sutherland). At the same time, Katniss also learns about a secret rebellion spreading throughout all of Panem -- a rebellion that will place her at the center of a plot to turn the tables on Snow.

Realizing the stakes are no longer just for survival, Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) teams up with her closest friends, including Peeta (Josh Hutcherson), Gale (Liam Hemsworth) and Finnick for the ultimate mission. Together, they leave District 13 to liberate the citizens of war-torn Panem and assassinate President Snow, who's obsessed with destroying Katniss. What lies ahead are mortal traps, dangerous enemies and moral choices that will ultimately determine the future of millions.

Northern Ireland, 1960: Father Thomas Riley and Father John Thornton are dispatched by the Vatican to investigate reports of a miracle, a statue of the Virgin Mary weeping blood, at a remote Catholic asylum for immoral women. Armed with 16mm film cameras to record their findings, the priests instead discover a depraved horror show of sadistic nuns, satanism and demonic possession. Supernatural forces are at work here, but they are not the doing of God.

Still recovering from the trauma of being kidnapped on the previous Halloween by the Blue Skeleton - a group that takes extreme haunt to another level - five friends decide they must face their fears to move on. Heading back out on the road to visit more haunted house attractions, new terror begins when signs of the Blue Skeleton start appearing again.
A woman finds a VHS tape that shows a series of gruesome tales.

Grace se despierta con un caso de amnesia y ve lo que ha sucedido con sus amigos después de que ella se ha ido durante años. Grace lucha por juntar las piezas del rompecabezas sobre lo que ha sucedido.
June se separa del grupo en un esfuerzo por recopilar cualquier información que ayude a detener una amenaza inminente.
Teddy mantiene prisionera a Alicia, que se reúne con viejos amigos y debe confrontar su pasado si quiere seguir adelante y escapar.

Todos luchan desesperadamente por encontrar una manera de afrontar la destrucción inminente en sus propios términos.

Un nuevo líder toma el control del Rancho. Daniel, por su parte, ayuda a Lola a distribuir el agua, pero cada vez quedan menos recursos disponibles.
Wherever your destination, traveling local or far, indoor or outdoor, you can be sure AccuWeather Weekend always has you covered.
Goes beyond the forecast to give you the how and why about stuff you wanted to ask about weather, space and science.

Decades after the abduction of his newborn twin, world-famous American pianist John Ma (Jackie Chan) arrives in Hong Kong to perform and finds himself face-to-face with Boomer (Jackie Chan), the identical twin brother he has never known. When the reunited brothers switch places by mistake, John discovers that Boomer is a petty criminal with a knack for getting into trouble. Soon John gets in over his head with a group of gangsters looking for Boomer, and his brother vows to save him.

After the parents of Ruby (Leelee Sobieski) and her younger brother, Rhett (Trevor Morgan), are killed in a car crash, their parents' best friends, Erin and Terry Glass (Diane Lane, Stellan Skarsgard), become their guardians. The children hear promises of a world of opulence and California fun -- all they have to do is move into the Glasses' gated house. Before very long, though, Ruby suspects that Erin and Terry may not be the ideal guardians they seemed to be.

When Suzanne wants a real honeymoon, Nick tries to plan an extravagant surprise, but despite his best efforts to create something romantic, instead misleads Suzanne into thinking he is cheating on her.

Nick struggles to prove himself when he is promoted to co-host alongside the lazy, arrogant Brick Street.

Everyone tries to resolve personal issues while stuck in line the morning of a Black Friday sale. Kevin anticipates buying a new video game, Lindsey meets a boy, relationship problems plague Martin and Terrence hopes to buy toys for charity.
Nick becomes a more influential parent, so he pushes Kevin and Lindsey hard, and they become model children.
Nick hesitantly attends his high school reunion, but all of his fears come true when his high school nickname haunts him throughout the event. Lindsey prepares a feast.
When Nick realises he is the same age his father was when he died, he decides not to waste another minute and starts tackling a list of risky activities to accomplish before he dies.
While hosting an awards ceremony, Nick gets laughs by making Suzanne the butt of his jokes, but finds he cannot stand the heat when Suzanne turns the tables and starts making fun of him in public.
Kevin is a big football fan, but Nick does not understand the appeal. Suzanne is frustrated by Lindsey's lack of communication and creates a fake Facebook account to learn what is going on.
When the family oversleeps on the morning Lindsey is set to sing the National Anthem at a baseball game, it is all hands on deck just to make it to out of the house on time.
Nick wants Lindsey and Kevin to give back to the community, so they select a charity they find online. But when the charity keeps asking for more money, Nick has to get to the bottom of it.
When Suzanne's Mother comes to visit, she attacks Nick for being an inadequate husband, while hiding her true feelings of her own husband's inadequacy, until Suzanne and Terrence press her.

Just being rich isn't enough to endure the teen oppression at Shinhwa -- loners are often marked as targets by the bored über-clique called F4.

Gardner Barnes is a young Texan who has just graduated from college and is unsure of what to do next. Along with his friends, collectively known as the Groovers, Gardner embarks on a road trip to the Rio Grande as a last hurrah for the group. As the trip progresses, Gardner and his buddies, including Kenneth Waggener and Phil Hicks, struggle with their impending adulthood and the looming issue of the Vietnam War.

Gus (Matt Dillon) is a New Yorker with an entrepreneurial spirit. He'd like to quit his job and open a bowling alley, but financial obligations from his ex-marriage are standing in his way. Gus owes alimony to Leonora (Annabella Sciorra), but if she remarries, he'll be flush with cash. So he embarks on a scheme to find her a husband. Leonora is in a relationship with Tom (William Hurt), but like Gus, she's a romantic -- and soon Gus and Leonora find they may still have a spark left.

Rising Hollywood screenwriter Peter Appleton (Jim Carrey) is blacklisted in the early 1950s Red Scare. Following a drunken car accident, he wakes with amnesia near the small town of Lawson, Calif., where the residents mistake him for Luke Trimble, a local boy declared missing in action during World War II. As Peter helps Luke's father (Martin Landau) and high school sweetheart (Laurie Holden) reopen the town's sole movie theater, questions arise about his true identity and motivations.

Joe Banks (Tom Hanks) is dying, apparently. This is good news, since his life was not much worth living anyway. On the upside, a strange millionaire (Lloyd Bridges) offers Joe a way to die with meaning and dignity: by hurling himself into a volcano. With plenty of spending cash and an ensemble of new luggage, Joe embarks on an absurdist journey to his demise, guided by two very disparate sisters, and trying to puzzle out the meaning of existence.

When a sheik (Jamie Farr) decides to sponsor a cross-country race in hope of winning, racer J.J. McClure (Burt Reynolds) enters the competition along with his friend Victor (Dom DeLuise). They aspire to claim the $1 million prize and pick up two women on the way. Meanwhile, the sheik helps Jamie Blake (Dean Martin) and Morris Fenderbaum (Sammy Davis Jr.) with an angry mob boss. But when the sheik is kidnapped, the contestants must come together to help him.

Former sportswriter Andy Farmer and his secretly aspiring author wife, Elizabeth, move to a small farm in Vermont, so Andy can focus on writing a novel. They quickly realize that the locals are not as welcoming as they'd like and that the farm is more distracting than inspiring. Having trouble with his manuscript, and with his marriage on the rocks, Andy is forced to take hilariously drastic measures in an attempt to get his life back on track.

Monty is back at Longmeadow, getting stuck into more seasonal tasks. Joe Swift heads to Houghton Lodge Gardens in Hampshire renowned for its walled kitchen garden and heritage fruit collection.

In the second of her films about botany, Carol Klein goes underground to unravel the mysteries of roots and why they are so important to the health of our plants. Joe Swift meets fashion icon, Dame Zandra Rhodes, to explore how the flowers she likes to grow have influenced her designs over the years.

Two gardeners, each living on their own, are hoping Monty can help them. In Blackpool, Alex dreams of turning her boring backyard into a magical enchanted forest. Also in Bristol, Ross has taken on a very over-grown allotment.

In Leyton, Tariq and Sairah want to turn their dumping ground of a backyard into a sumptuous award-winning garden, suitable for entertaining friends and family. Both have competitive jobs in the banking sector and are used to winning at work but when it comes to gardening, they don't know where to begin.

One couple battle to turn a clay-clogged building site in Sussex into a piece of Portugal. Another tackle a forest of overgrowth in their new back garden in Cadeby. They are determined to create a productive space, something they have always wanted.

Monty continues his travels to learn about the art of Japanese stonemasonry and the famous tea ceremonies and their accompanying gardens, before finally taking a lesson in the delicate art of traditional flower arranging.

Monty Don returns to Japan during the fiery blaze of autumn. He visits the three great gardens of Japan to learn how they protect the garden from the coming winter and learns how the Japanese are weaving nature into their concrete urban jungle.

Monty Don conducts a personal grand tour around Italy's magnificent gardens from the luxurious retreats of the moneyed north to the lavish hideaways of the romantic south. In this episode, he's in and around Rome, a power base of emperors and popes, to explore gardens that are among some of the most extravagant and flamboyant ever created in history.

Monty Don is on a grand tour around Italy, this time visiting gardens both in Florence and around the sun-scorched Tuscan countryside. Monty discovers how, like a piece of sculpture, renaissance gardens were created as works of art, and how a group of Edwardian ex-pats mistakenly reinforced the idea that formal Italian gardens were flowerless.

Monty Don continues his grand garden tour of Italy. This time he is in Naples to visit some of the most sublime, romantic retreats in southern Italy. After all the formality of the green gardens around Rome and Florence, Monty seeks out idyllic horticultural gems set against the dramatic scenery of the Amalfi Coast to discover why, in the south, gardens are informal and, above all, filled with flowers.

Monty Don concludes his garden tour of Italy in the wealthy north where, in the Veneto and Lucca, extravagant pleasure gardens were created for flirtation and fun. In the Lakes, Monty meets up with the garden society, the Grandi Giardini Italiani, to peer over the fence at luxurious creations of the rich and famous. The journey ends on Lake Maggiore to see the most theatrical horticultural gem of Italy.

With autumn on the horizon, the seasonal planting of bulbs for spring-flowering begins at Longmeadow. Jeremy's pork sando with homemade tonkatsu sauce; Joe tries his hand at crispy chili beef; Jeremy cooks up scallops on the shore of Loch Ewe, while his sticky toffee pudding takes things to another level.

It is main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. As the barbecues are fired up, all eight chefs are feeling the heat. The judges are joined by guest judge Gordon Reid.

It is dessert day and with just one place remaining at the 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon banquet, each chef is giving everything they have got. The judges are joined by guest judge Annabel Croft, former British number one and Junior 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon champion.
It's the grand finale and the winning chefs must now cook their dishes at the banquet. Once in the kitchen, the chefs face the huge challenge of scaling up their dishes.

Competing for top spot are Danny Parker, head chef at Michelin starred 'House of Tides' in Newcastle, who is back to try his luck in the competition again after being knocked out in the regional heat last year following a tense tie-break. He's taking on two newcomers: Dan Fletcher, protégé of Phil Howard, and now head chef at 'Fenchurch' in the City of London, and David Coulson, who runs 'Peace and Loaf' in Newcastle, which boasts 2 AA rosettes.

After a tense starter course the chefs are all aiming for 10s with their unique fish dishes. David is celebrating a personal connection to the brief with his `My Cod I Bet Me Ma'am Has Seen Some Trotters', a tribute to his mum who has worked as a chiropodist. Dan's `For All Those Sleepless Nights' pays tribute to night shift workers from the NHS with some bold but classic flavours while Danny's `Not All Superheroes Wear Capes' aims to give a taste of luxury to the hardworking staff.

Dan pays tribute to an icon of modern nursing, Florence Nightingale, while Danny is inspired by the founder of the NHS, Aneurin Bevan. David's dish is dedicated to the air ambulance staff who saved the life of his fiancé, and he even takes a trip to meet one of them.

It's the chefs' last chance to impress and tensions are high. Dan takes a risk with an unusual combination of ewe's milk and bergamot while Danny is determined to pull out all the stops with his complex dessert `Aunty Gwen's Chocolate'. David hopes to transform a childhood comfort classic into a show stopping dessert. Dan also takes a trip to meet Dr Ben Clarke who was working in the Royal London Hospital A&E during the London Bridge terror attack.
The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Banquet champion Selin Kiazim, a rising star of the London scene renowned for her Turkish Cypriot fusion flavours, is back hoping to join the elite group of chefs who have made it to the banquet twice. She is up against James Cochran who's worked at some of London's toughest kitchens including 2 Michelin starred 'The Ledbury' and Scott Goss from 'The Twenty Six' in Tunbridge Wells, renowned for his use of local Kent ingredients.

The chefs do battle for the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen is tense. Lobster is catch of the day for James whose dish is Caribbean-inspired. Scott is attempting to elevate a classic fish pie, dedicated to his mum who worked as a pharmacist in the NHS for 23 years. And Selin is taking a risk with a complex three-part fish dish featuring sardines, scallops and langoustines, as a nod to the purported health benefits of a Mediterranean diet.

Scott is showcasing rare-breed Tamworth pork to say thank you to the rare breed of people who work for the NHS. Selin is serving a complex duck dish using ingredients from all around the world to honour `Our Global NHS'. And James is presenting five cuts of goat cooked in five different ways, for his bold dish `Under The Knife'.

Selin puts her own unique twist on tea and toast. James creates a decadent coconut parfait accompanied by mango purée filled doughnuts for his dessert 'Tree of Life' inspired by the coconut palm tree, the NHS and both of their contributions to our health. Scott hopes his elevated gypsy tart 'Honey Bee Good' will secure him a place in the final.
The two remaining London and the south-east chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they remake their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Vying to be crowned champion of Scotland are three newcomers to the GBM kitchen. Lorna McNee is a former Scottish Chef of the Year and is renowned for her technical precision, gained from working at two-Michelin-starred restaurant 'Andrew Fairlie'.

It is the fish course and the chefs are all out to impress. The heat is increased as all three serve their unique takes on lobster. Ross seeks victory with his dish 'Lobster Aid'. Lorna's 'Live Well, Live Very Well' features only three elements.

Ross is attempting to elevate a classic into a dish worthy of the banquet, Lorna is cooking a personal tribute to NHS staff using unusual yuzu and tonka bean flavours, and Ben is serving an experimental dish which includes a beeswax ice cream.

It is judging day and the two remaining chefs must impress the panel of Oliver Peyton, Andi Oliver and Matthew Fort. Both chefs are gunning for success and are doing everything they can to deliver their menus to perfection.

Three chefs compete in the heat for the central region. Returner Ryan Simson-Trotman, who failed to reach the national finals last year, is originally from Nuneaton and opened his own restaurant Orwells in the Oxfordshire countryside with his partner Liam, who is also a contestant in the North West region.

Germany took just four weeks to conquer Poland, using a new form of warfare, Blitzkrieg. Six armoured tank units known as Panzer divisions, supported by the Luftwaffe, quickly broke through Polish defences.

After the retreat from Dunkirk, Churchill rallied Britain in its darkest hour. Hitler was only just across the channel, but he reckoned without our supreme strategist, the might of the navy and the manoeuvrability of the air force.

As a young cop, Erin Bell went undercover to infiltrate a gang in the California desert -- with tragic results. Bell continues to work as a detective for the Los Angeles Police Department, but feelings of anger and remorse leave her worn-down and consumed by guilt. When the leader of that gang suddenly re-emerges, Erin embarks on an obsessive quest to find his former associates, bring him to justice and make peace with her tortured past.

A former assassin, known simply as The Bride (Uma Thurman), wakes from a coma four years after her jealous ex-lover Bill (David Carradine) attempts to murder her on her wedding day. Fueled by an insatiable desire for revenge, she vows to get even with every person who contributed to the loss of her unborn child, her entire wedding party, and four years of her life. After devising a hit list, The Bride sets off on her quest, enduring unspeakable injury and unscrupulous enemies.

The Bride (Uma Thurman) picks up where she left off in volume one with her quest to finish the hit list she has composed of all the people who have wronged her, including ex-boyfriend Bill (David Carradine), who tried to have her killed four years ago during her wedding to another man. Leaving several dead in her wake, she eventually tracks down Bill in Mexico. Using skills she has learned during her assassin career, she attempts to finish what she set out to do in the first place.

One of the wagons attached to a wagon train has a damaged axle. Because the train has a strict schedule to follow, the broken wagon is left behind. Jason Clay (Lance Fuller) and Tobias Taylor (Chill Wills) repair the axle, and the situation appears to be remedied. But then the wagon crew runs into a bigger problem -- they are in Comanche territory, and the Comanche refuse to let them pass unless they hand over the hundred Kentucky rifles on board.

Buffalo hide trader Tom Doan comes to the aid of Jude Pilchuk, a fellow hunter whose wagon was run off the trail by white thieves disguised as raiding American Indians. Doan and Pilchuk investigate and discover that Randall Jett-- the abusive father of Doan's love interest Milly Fayre-- is to blame. When Jett then kidnaps Milly and disappears into the wild, Doan must track down and outsmart Jett's gang to save the woman he loves.

Fresh out of college, American Rod Drew (John Wayne) is asked to assist in the search for missing people in Canada. Accompanied by Wabi (Noah Beery Jr.), his friend from school, Drew travels north, but quickly gets into a confrontation with a gang of French Canadian outlaws. When the bandits abduct the young Felice Newsome (Verna Hillie), it becomes apparent they're responsible for the other disappearances as well. Luckily, Drew and Wabi are there, determined to find and free the captives.

Jerry Mason (John Wayne), fresh out of college back East, heads home to Texas to join a blacksmith business with family friend Jake (George Hayes). But when they discover a gold nugget in a horseshoe, they're led down a dangerous path, as crooks Joe Cole (Yakima Canutt) and Harris (Lloyd Whitlock) scheme to take the rock from the unsuspecting Jerry and Jake. This ultimately gets Jake shot and wounded, lands Jerry in jail unjustly and leaves the pair plotting to get revenge on the criminals.

Majesty Hammond (Jo Ann Sayers) has just met rancher Gene Stewart (Victor Jory), but they're already headed to the altar. Though preoccupied by her own relationship, Majesty also wants to break up a romance between her brother, Al (Russell Hayden), and reputed floozy Flo (Ruth Rogers). As things get increasingly complicated at home, Gene goes to Mexico to fight in the revolution. But, when love summons him back home, he and Majesty will be involved in a battle against local corruption.

Another shooting draws Horse's future son-in-law, Pat Farrell (John Archer), into the mystery.
